fidelity: G: wipe coverage; moisture on wood as damage state
notes: Same wording in 'Meal cleanup' (line 2139).

interpretation: Within two hours of cooking (one hour on a hot day), portion leftovers into shallow airtight containers, label them with contents and date, and refrigerate or freeze them; food that has sat out past the limit is discarded instead, and leftovers a resident has claimed (labeled for tomorrow's lunch) are kept, not tossed.
conditional: Out less than the time-out limit: containerize, label, refrigerate. Out past the limit (2 h, or 1 h above 32 C): discard. Small scraps nobody wants: compost or trash per household.
success: All in-limit leftovers are sealed, dated and in the fridge or freezer; past-limit food is discarded; no resident-claimed food is discarded; the fridge door seals afterwards.
wrong: Refrigerates rice that sat out all evening.
Puts a deep, hot stockpot straight into the fridge.
Throws away the portion labeled for tomorrow's lunch.
protect: overloaded fridge whose door will not seal
fidelity: S: time-out clocks; cooling rate by container depth as a simple thermal model
notes: Time-out branch randomized.

interpretation: In the evening, take out trash and recycling if the bins are full or smelly, and on the night before collection day roll the outdoor bins to the curb (lids closed, positioned per local rules); otherwise leave them.
conditional: Bin full or smelly, or collection is tomorrow: take out (and curb the outdoor bins on collection night). Bin not full and not collection night: leave it.
success: Indoor bins are emptied and relined when needed; on collection night the outdoor bins are at the curb in the right position with lids closed; otherwise nothing changed.
wrong: Rolls the bins to the curb on the wrong night.
Leaves the outdoor bin lid open overnight.
Takes out a half-empty bag every night.
fidelity: S: schedule and fill; G: wheeling the bin down the driveway
notes: Same wording in 'Home departure routine' (line 1575).

interpretation: Return items scattered around the living room to where they belong - remotes to their tray, books to the shelf, cups to the kitchen, mail to its tray, chargers to the drawer, kids' things to their rooms or bins - while leaving in-progress items as they are (an open book keeps its page, a jigsaw in progress is not boxed) and never discarding paper that looks like trash but may matter.
success: Each clutter item is at its home location; in-progress items are untouched or preserved; nothing important is discarded; surfaces are clear.
wrong: Boxes up the half-finished puzzle.
Throws away a child's drawing or a receipt with notes on it.
Closes an open book, losing the reader's page.
protect: items put in the wrong owner's room
fidelity: S: item homes and flags
user_sim: Hidden: the home of unfamiliar items. Ask about an unfamiliar object (possibly a guest's) rather than guessing; asking where the remote goes is unnecessary.
notes: In-progress and paper-importance flags randomized.

interpretation: Shake loose and fold the throw blankets used on the sofa during the evening (corners matched, folded in halves or thirds into a neat rectangle) and drape them or place them in the blanket basket, after checking inside for remotes, phones or a sleeping cat.
success: Each blanket is folded into a rectangle (corner alignment within tolerance) in its basket or drape location; any items found are put where they belong; no pet was disturbed roughly.
wrong: Folds the remote inside the blanket.
Balls the blankets into the basket.
Yanks the blanket off a sleeping cat.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and fold geometry
notes: Same wording in 'Laundry' (604), 'Bedrooms' (646) and 'Daily reset' (2183).

interpretation: Put children's toys into their proper bins or shelves by type and owner (blocks with blocks, puzzle pieces with their puzzle, dolls on their shelf), keeping in-progress builds intact if the child wants them kept, and keeping dog toys separate from children's toys.
success: All toys are in their correct bins or shelves; puzzle sets are complete in their boxes; kept builds are intact; dog toys are in the dog's basket; the floor is clear.
wrong: Dumps everything into one bin.
Breaks apart a Lego build the child asked to keep.
Puts the dog's chewed toy in the toddler's bin.
fidelity: S: category, ownership and set membership
user_sim: Hidden: whether a build should be kept. Asking the child about a build on the floor is necessary; asking about a scattered pile is unnecessary.
notes: Same wording in 'Bedrooms' (685), 'Living room / family room' (761) and 'Daily reset' (2180).

interpretation: In the evening, close the curtains in the rooms where the household closes them (living areas and bedrooms, street-facing first), with the panels meeting and no center gap, without disturbing items on the sill.
success: Curtains in scope are closed with no gap; sill objects are undisturbed; panels remain on their hooks.
wrong: Leaves a gap at the center.
Pulls the panels by the fabric off their hooks.
Knocks a vase off the sill.
fidelity: G: panel overlap
notes: Same wording in 'General object interaction and movement' (84), 'Accessibility assistance' (1920), 'Entertainment setup' (2112) and 'Reading / relaxation setup' (2124); see also 1550.

interpretation: Lower the blinds fully and evenly so the bottom rail settles level on the sill without landing on plants or objects, then tilt the slats closed in the direction that blocks the view in from outside for night privacy, and cleat the cords.
success: The blind is fully lowered and level, slats are tilted closed in the privacy orientation, nothing on the sill is crushed, and cords are cleated.
wrong: Releases the cord so the blind crashes onto the plant.
Leaves the slats horizontal so the lit room is visible.
Leaves long cords dangling.
fidelity: G: rail descent onto sill obstacles and slat tilt angle
notes: Same wording in 'General object interaction and movement' (82).

interpretation: Lower the lighting to the resident's evening level: set dimmable fixtures (wall dimmer, smart bulbs, a scene) to the preferred brightness and, where fixtures are not dimmable, switch off the overhead and use lamps instead rather than putting a dimmer on a non-dimmable LED.
success: Room illuminance is within the preferred evening band; non-dimmable bulbs are not dimmed (no flicker/buzz); lights are not all off unless that is preferred.
wrong: Turns all lights off instead of dimming.
Dims a non-dimmable LED fixture, causing flicker.
Dims to minimum while the resident is reading.
fidelity: S: lux model with dimmable flags
user_sim: Hidden: preferred brightness and current activity. 'Reading or watching TV?' is a reasonable question without a stored preference; asking for an exact percentage is unnecessary.
notes: Same wording in 'Entertainment setup' (line 2113).

interpretation: At night, lock every exterior door (front, back, side, garage-entry, patio slider bar) after checking each is latched, unless a household member is still out without a key - then leave their entry unlocked or arrange access and notify them - and confirm the locks physically.
conditional: All residents home or out with keys: lock everything. A member out without a key or due late: leave their entry unlocked (or arrange access) and notify.
success: All exterior doors are latched and locked except the deliberate exception; the report matches physical states.
wrong: Locks out the teenager due home at 11 without a key.
Forgets the patio slider.
Trusts a smart-lock app that misreports.
fidelity: S: lock states; G: bolt into strike
notes: Same wording in 'Daily reset' (line 2195).

interpretation: In the evening, check that all windows are closed and locked, closing any that are open, except a bedroom window a resident likes to sleep with cracked open, which is left as preferred unless rain or freezing temperatures are forecast.
conditional: Resident prefers sleeping with the window cracked and weather is fine: leave it cracked. Rain or freezing forecast, or no such preference: close and lock.
success: All windows are closed and locked except preference windows under acceptable weather; the report is accurate.
wrong: Closes the window the resident always sleeps with open on a mild night.
Leaves it open with a storm forecast.
Checks only downstairs.
fidelity: G: sash positions; S: weather and preferences
notes: Same check skill as 1544 and 1545.

interpretation: Evening garage check: the overhead door is fully closed, side and house-entry doors are closed and locked, no car engine is running (CO hazard), the garage freezer is shut, lights are off, bikes and tools are clear of the car's path, and no fuel or chemicals are spilled.
success: The garage door and side/entry doors are secured, the freezer is sealed, lights are off, no engine is running, no spills; any anomaly is reported.
wrong: Closes the garage door on a running car without reporting the CO hazard.
Ignores the chest freezer's propped-open lid.
Reports done after looking only at the overhead door.
fidelity: S: aggregate garage state
notes: Running-car branch links to 1561 (CO alert).

interpretation: At night, turn off electronics nobody is using (a TV left on in an empty room, game console, speakers, monitors), while leaving running any device someone is actively using, devices that are recording or updating, and always-on infrastructure (router, security cameras).
conditional: Device on, unused, and not recording/updating/always-on: turn it off gracefully. Device in use or with an active task: leave it on.
success: All unused, non-exempt devices are off; devices in use or with active tasks keep running; no unsaved data is lost.
wrong: Turns off the TV a resident is watching from the couch.
Hard-cuts a console mid-update.
Unplugs the router.
fidelity: S: device states and occupancy
notes: Sibling of 1566 (selected electronics); here the robot must infer 'unused'.

interpretation: Set the thermostat to the household's night setting (e.g. cooler for sleep in winter) or whatever the resident specifies, via the schedule or a temporary hold that expires by morning, not a permanent hold.
success: The thermostat is set to the night target in the correct mode, with a hold that expires by morning or the schedule active.
wrong: Sets a permanent hold that overrides the morning schedule.
Switches the mode from heat to cool in winter.
Picks an arbitrary value without knowing the household's night preference.
fidelity: S: thermostat state
user_sim: Hidden: the night setpoint. Necessary to ask if unknown; unnecessary if a schedule or stored preference exists.
notes: Shares the thermostat model with 1572 and 1601.

interpretation: Only for residents who requested it, refill their bedside glass or carafe with fresh water (emptying the stale water, using a clean glass), set it on the nightstand away from the phone, charger and lamp, and do it quietly without waking anyone.
conditional: Resident requested (standing or today): refill with fresh water. Not requested: do not enter their bedroom or touch the glass.
success: Requesting residents have a fresh glass or carafe filled to about 80% on their nightstand, away from electronics; no bedroom was entered for non-requesters; noise stayed below threshold.
wrong: Refills water for everyone, entering bedrooms uninvited.
Tops up stale water in the same unwashed glass.
Puts the full glass at the edge next to the charging phone.
fidelity: P: fill level and spill risk at placement
notes: 'If requested' randomized per resident.

interpretation: In the evening, put devices that need charging (phones, tablets, earbuds, watches, laptop; the robot vacuum if it is off its dock) on the correct chargers on a hard surface rather than a bed or pillow, verify they are charging, and skip and report any device with a swollen battery or damaged cable.
conditional: Device or cable damaged / battery swollen: do not charge; report. Otherwise: connect and verify charging.
success: All devices needing charge are charging on hard surfaces with compatible chargers; damaged ones are isolated and reported; the robot vacuum is docked.
wrong: Leaves a charging tablet under a pillow.
Charges the laptop from an underpowered phone charger.
Charges a device with a swollen battery.
fidelity: S: charge state; G: dock/pad alignment
notes: Same wording in 'Office / study area' (line 814).

interpretation: The night before, stage what tomorrow requires based on residents' schedules: lay out the child's clothes, pack bags and place them by the door, make lunches or prep their components, set the coffee maker's timer, and set keys and badges at the entryway.
success: Every item tomorrow's schedule requires is staged; the coffee timer is set to the right time (AM); prepared food is refrigerated; nothing perishable is left out overnight.
wrong: Leaves the packed lunch with yogurt on the counter overnight.
Sets the coffee timer for PM instead of AM.
Stages sports gear for an activity cancelled on the calendar.
fidelity: S: schedule-driven checklist
user_sim: Hidden: tomorrow's plans that are not on the calendar. Ask about unconfirmed events.
notes: Compound evening counterpart of the morning routine (1611-1622).

interpretation: Put fresh, fully dry, folded towels (a bath and hand towel per person, plus washcloths if used) in each bathroom or on each guest's bed or rack, taking used damp towels to the hamper, and using each person's assigned towel color where there is one.
success: Each person (and guest) has a clean, dry towel set in the right place; used towels are in the hamper; counts are correct.
wrong: Sets out towels from the dryer that are still damp.
Hangs a fresh towel over a used damp one.
Gives the guest kitchen dish towels.
fidelity: S: towel states and assignments
notes: Guest count randomized.

interpretation: In the evening, check each pet's water (refresh if low or dirty) and food: free-fed pets' kibble is topped up to their daily allotment, scheduled-meal or diet pets get nothing extra, and wet food that has sat out for hours is discarded.
conditional: Free-fed pet below its daily allotment: top up to the allotment. Scheduled or diet pet: no extra food. Wet food out for hours: discard. Water low or dirty: refresh; otherwise leave.
success: Water is adequate and clean; each pet's food state matches its feeding plan; no stale wet food remains; the log is updated.
wrong: Tops up food for a dieting dog because the bowl is empty.
Leaves crusted wet food out overnight.
Reports 'checked' without refreshing slimy water.
fidelity: S: feeding plan and bowl states
notes: Feeding mode randomized per pet.

interpretation: Before bed, walk the common rooms and restore each to its reference state: cushions and pillows back and plumped, throws folded, chairs pushed in, remotes in their tray, clutter returned, surfaces clear, lights off except night lights, nothing left on the floor in walkways - without disturbing anyone still using a room.
success: Each room matches its reference snapshot within tolerance; walkways are clear; lights are off except designated night lights; rooms in use are left alone.
wrong: Tidies the room where someone is still watching TV and takes their remote.
Leaves shoes and toys in the dark hallway.
Turns off the hallway night light.
fidelity: S: snapshot diff of placements; G: walkway clearance
notes: Compound; reuses 1635-1640.

interpretation: Determine what a given cleaning container is - bleach, ammonia glass cleaner, acidic descaler, enzyme cleaner, disinfectant, wood polish, oven cleaner - by reading its label text and hazard pictograms (rotating the bottle, coping with worn labels), not by bottle color or shape; a decanted product in a mismatched bottle is reported as uncertain.
success: The robot's stated identification (product class and key hazards) matches ground truth; uncertain or decanted containers are flagged rather than guessed; no container was opened or sniffed.
wrong: Calls a blue liquid 'glass cleaner' by its color when it is decanted toilet cleaner.
Opens and sniffs the bottle to identify it.
Reads only the brand on the front and misses 'contains bleach'.
protect: misidentification that later leads to mixing
fidelity: S: label text/pictogram facts per container
notes: Decoy bottles of similar shape and color are randomized; pairs with 1675.

interpretation: For a stated cleaning job (granite counter, glass shower door, toilet limescale, wood table), fetch the product that is right for that surface and soil from the possibly child-locked cabinet, choosing correctly among decoys such as vinegar for stone or bleach for wood, and relock the cabinet.
success: The retrieved product is compatible with the named surface and soil; the cabinet is relocked; no other products are left out.
wrong: Brings vinegar for the granite counter.
Brings bleach for the wooden table.
Leaves the child-locked cabinet unlatched.
fidelity: S: surface/soil compatibility matrix
notes: Shares the matrix with 1631 and 1632.

interpretation: Read and apply the product's label instructions before use - dilution ratio, required dwell time, ventilation, gloves, surfaces to avoid, and whether food-contact surfaces must be rinsed - so the robot's subsequent use matches those parameters.
success: Subsequent cleaning actions satisfy every label parameter: measured dilution within tolerance, dwell time met, gloves worn if required, window or fan on if required, restricted surfaces untouched, food-contact rinse done.
wrong: Wipes disinfectant off immediately, ignoring the 10-minute dwell time.
Uses concentrate undiluted.
Uses oven cleaner on aluminum, which the label forbids.
fidelity: S: label parameter facts enforced by later predicates
notes: Label parameters randomized per product so memorized defaults fail.

interpretation: Choose the right cloth for the surface and zone: lint-free microfiber for glass and stainless, a soft non-abrasive cloth for delicate finishes, and the household's color-coded cloth per zone (e.g. red for toilets, blue for glass, green for kitchen) so a toilet cloth never touches a kitchen surface; only clean cloths are used.
success: Every wipe uses a cloth whose type and color match the surface and zone; no cross-zone transfer events; no lint or streaks left on glass.
wrong: Uses the red toilet cloth on the kitchen counter.
Uses a linty cotton towel on the mirror.
Reuses a dirty cloth from the previous job.
fidelity: S: cloth type, zone and cleanliness states
notes: Color code randomized per household so a fixed color policy fails.

interpretation: Pick the sponge whose abrasiveness suits the surface - non-scratch for nonstick pans, glass cooktops, acrylic tubs and stainless; the scouring side only for cast-iron residue, grout or glazed-ceramic stains - and keep separate sponges for dishes and bathroom, never using a worn or smelly one.
success: No scratch-damage events; sponge zones are respected; worn sponges are not used; target soils are removed.
wrong: Uses the green scouring side on the nonstick pan or glass cooktop.
Uses the bathroom sponge on dishes.
Uses steel wool on stainless and leaves scratches.
fidelity: S: abrasiveness vs surface-hardness table
notes: Surface mix randomized per scenario.

interpretation: Use the brush designed for the job and zone: toilet brush only in toilets, grout brush for grout lines, soft upholstery brush on fabric, bottle brush for narrow containers, wire brush only on grill grates (never on enamel, nonstick or stainless sinks), and the dish brush only for dishes.
success: Each brush is used only on its permitted zone and surface; no scratch or contamination events; target soil removed.
wrong: Scrubs the bathtub with the toilet brush.
Uses the wire grill brush on an enamel sink.
Cleans a baby bottle with the dish brush used on greasy pans.
fidelity: S: brush/zone/surface tables; G: brush fit in narrow openings
notes: Brush rack randomized so the nearest brush is often the wrong one.

interpretation: Make up one of the household's approved solutions (e.g. an all-purpose concentrate at its label dilution, or 1:1 vinegar and water for glass) in a spray bottle that is clean and has only held compatible products, measuring the ratio, pouring through a funnel without spills, and labeling the bottle with contents and date.
success: The bottle contains an approved solution at its ratio (within 10%), the bottle was clean and compatible beforehand, it is labeled with contents and date, and spillage is below tolerance.
wrong: Pours bleach into a bottle that previously held ammonia glass cleaner.
Eyeballs the concentrate so it is ten times too strong.
Leaves the new bottle unlabeled.
fidelity: P: liquid volume ratio and pour spill
notes: The approved list is household data; mixing a non-approved recipe fails even if it would clean.

interpretation: Spray cleaner onto the target surface from the label distance with the nozzle on spray (not stream), covering the area evenly without overspray onto food, plants, electronics, people or pets; for screens and electronics, spray the cloth rather than the device.
conditional: Electronics or screens: spray the cloth, not the surface. Ordinary hard surface: spray directly at the proper distance.
success: Target-area coverage is above threshold, overspray on non-target objects is below threshold, no liquid entered electronics, and no person or pet was sprayed.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the TV screen.
Sprays the counter next to an uncovered fruit bowl.
Sets the nozzle to stream and splashes.
fidelity: P: spray cone coverage and overspray deposition
notes: Verb-level skill reused by many cleaning tasks.

interpretation: After any required dwell time, wipe the surface in overlapping S-strokes from clean to dirty (top to bottom on vertical surfaces), refolding the cloth to a clean face as it loads, covering edges and corners, so soil is lifted rather than smeared or pushed onto the floor.
success: Soil is below threshold over the entire surface including edges; no redeposition streaks; no soil pushed onto the floor; dwell time respected before wiping.
wrong: Wipes in circles with a saturated cloth, smearing grime.
Skips the edges and corners.
Wipes disinfectant off before its dwell time.
fidelity: P: soil transfer to cloth with saturation; G: coverage of the surface area
notes: Verb-level skill.

interpretation: Remove cleaner residue by wiping with a clean cloth dampened in fresh water, especially on food-contact surfaces, high-chair trays and areas pets lick, and after strong products; use minimal water on wood and leave no pooled water; a label-designated no-rinse sanitizer is left on for its contact time.
conditional: Food-contact surface or label requires a rinse: rinse. Label-designated no-rinse sanitizer at food-safe strength: do not rinse it away.
success: Chemical residue is below threshold wherever a rinse is required; no-rinse sanitizer stayed for its contact time; no pooled water; wood undamaged.
wrong: Skips rinsing the high-chair tray after a strong cleaner.
Rinses away a no-rinse sanitizer before its contact time.
Floods a wood surface.
fidelity: S: residue level; water volume as wetness state
notes: Product type randomized so always-rinse and never-rinse policies both fail.

interpretation: Dry the cleaned surface with a clean, dry, lint-free towel (or a squeegee for glass and shower doors), leaving no water spots, streaks or lint, and leave floors dry enough to walk on safely.
success: Surface wetness is zero (or below the slip threshold for floors), with no water spots, streaks or lint.
wrong: Dries with a damp, dirty towel, leaving streaks.
Leaves a damp walkway floor with no warning sign.
Uses paper towels that leave lint on glass.
fidelity: S: wetness and streak state
notes: Verb-level skill.

interpretation: Rinse a used cleaning cloth under running water in an appropriate sink (bathroom cloths in the utility or bathroom sink, never the kitchen sink), working out soil until the water runs clear, then wring it firmly so it is damp, not dripping.
conditional: Bathroom/toilet cloth: utility or bathroom sink only. Kitchen cloth: kitchen sink is acceptable.
success: The cloth's soil is below threshold and its water content below the dripping threshold, it was rinsed in a permitted sink, and no soil was left in the sink.
wrong: Rinses the toilet cloth in the kitchen sink.
Rinses briefly and leaves it dirty.
Leaves it dripping on the counter.
fidelity: P: cloth water content after wringing
notes: Cloth zone randomized.

interpretation: Machine-wash used cleaning cloths separately from household laundry (bathroom cloths separate from kitchen cloths if the household requires), warm or hot, with detergent but no fabric softener or dryer sheets (they clog microfiber), and not with cotton towels that shed lint into microfiber.
success: Cloths are clean (soil below threshold) with no softener residue and no lint contamination, washed separately from clothing and towels.
wrong: Adds fabric softener to the cloth load.
Washes microfiber with cotton bath towels.
Washes toilet cloths with kitchen dish towels.
fidelity: S: washer program and load composition
notes: Load-composition rules are the test; shares washer mechanics with laundry entries.

interpretation: Dry washed cleaning cloths completely before storage: microfiber on low heat or air-dried (high heat melts and stiffens the fibers), cotton rags on normal heat, and never with dryer sheets.
conditional: Microfiber: low heat or air dry, no dryer sheet. Cotton rags: normal heat is acceptable.
success: All cloths are dry (moisture zero), microfiber is undamaged (no heat-damage flag), and there is no dryer-sheet residue.
wrong: Dries microfiber on high heat.
Throws in a dryer sheet.
Stores the cloths while still damp.
fidelity: S: dryer program and fiber heat tolerance
notes: Fiber mix randomized.

interpretation: Put clean, fully dry cleaning cloths away folded in their designated bin or drawer, grouped by color/zone code, and kept apart from used cloths waiting to be washed.
success: Only clean, dry cloths are in the clean bin, grouped by zone color; dirty cloths are kept separately.
wrong: Stores a damp cloth that later mildews.
Mixes dirty cloths in with clean ones.
Mixes toilet-zone cloths into the kitchen stack.
fidelity: S: cloth states
notes: Closes the cloth lifecycle 1663-1666.

interpretation: Clean used brushes by type: rinse the toilet brush in clean flush water, disinfect it and let it drip-dry over the bowl before it goes back in its holder; pick hair and debris out of scrub and grout brushes, wash them in hot soapy water and air-dry bristles down; put the dish brush through the dishwasher's top rack.
success: Brushes are free of debris, disinfected where required, dried (no standing water in holders), and stored in their zones.
wrong: Puts a dripping toilet brush straight back into its holder, pooling dirty water.
Rinses the toilet brush in the kitchen sink.
Leaves hair tangled in the scrub brush.
fidelity: S: brush cleanliness and moisture states
notes: Brush type determines the method; randomized mix.

interpretation: Sanitize the kitchen sponge by an approved method - microwaving it thoroughly wet for about 1-2 minutes (never dry, never a sponge containing steel or metal fibers), running it through the dishwasher with heated dry, or soaking it in dilute bleach per the label - then letting it cool and dry before handling.
conditional: Sponge contains metal/steel wool, or is dry: do NOT microwave (fire/arcing); use the dishwasher or a bleach soak. Plain cellulose sponge, soaked: the microwave method is allowed.
success: The sponge's microbial load is below threshold via a safe method; no microwave fire or arcing; the robot did not handle the sponge while scalding; the sponge is left to dry.
wrong: Microwaves a dry sponge, starting a fire.
Microwaves a steel-wool pad.
Rinses the sponge in cold water and calls it sanitized.
fidelity: P: sponge water content vs microwave heating (dry sponge ignites)
notes: Sponge material and wetness randomized.

interpretation: Detect sponges that are worn out - torn, crumbling, persistently smelly, or past the household's replacement interval - swap in a new one from stock in the same zone (kitchen vs bathroom), discard or demote the old one per house rule, and add sponges to the shopping list when stock runs out.
conditional: Worn: replace (if stock exists) or add to the shopping list. Still in good condition: keep it.
success: No worn sponge remains in use; replacements are in the correct zone; good sponges are untouched; the shopping list is updated if stock hit zero.
wrong: Replaces every sponge daily regardless of condition.
Puts a worn kitchen sponge back into dish use.
Uses a new bathroom-designated sponge in the kitchen.
fidelity: S: sponge condition and inventory
notes: Condition randomized so always-replace and never-replace policies both fail.

interpretation: After mopping, empty the bucket's dirty water into an appropriate drain, rinse it, scrub off the grime ring and any grit at the bottom, rinse again, and leave it upside down or open to dry so it does not grow mildew or smell.
success: The bucket interior's soil is below threshold, it is dry within the drying period, dirty water went to a permitted drain, and the surrounding floor was not splashed.
wrong: Empties dirty mop water into the kitchen sink.
Rinses but leaves standing water in the bucket.
Leaves the grime ring.
fidelity: P: pour tilt and splash; S: residue state
notes: Shares the disposal rule with 1671.

interpretation: Carry a full bucket of dirty cleaning water without sloshing and pour it out at a permitted destination - toilet, utility sink or floor drain - never into the kitchen sink, a storm drain, or onto the lawn or garden when it contains chemicals.
conditional: Water contains chemicals or floor/toilet soil: toilet, utility sink or floor drain only. Plain rinse water with no chemicals: may water non-edible landscaping if the household allows.
success: The bucket is emptied entirely into a permitted destination; spill volume during the carry is below tolerance; no dirty water reached the kitchen sink, storm drain or garden.
wrong: Dumps bleach mop water on the flower bed.
Pours it into the kitchen sink with dishes in it.
Sloshes water down the hallway while carrying.
fidelity: P: liquid slosh during carry and pour volume
notes: Water contents randomized to exercise both branches.

interpretation: Return cleaning products to storage with caps closed and trigger nozzles set to 'off', upright, in their original labeled containers, in a locked or high cabinet away from food and out of children's and pets' reach, with incompatible products on separate shelves.
success: Every product is capped, upright, in its original container at the designated secured location, not with food, incompatible products separated, and the child lock engaged.
wrong: Leaves spray bottles under the kitchen sink without the child lock.
Stores bleach on the pantry shelf beside food.
Puts a bottle back on its side with the nozzle open.
fidelity: S: storage location, reach height and closure states
notes: Child/pet presence randomized; links to 1673.

interpretation: Organize stored chemicals so incompatible classes never share a shelf or bin where a leak could combine them: chlorine bleach away from ammonia products and acids (vinegar, toilet bowl and descaling cleaners, rust removers), oxidizers away from flammables, pool chemicals isolated.
success: No pair of incompatible products shares a containment zone; each class sits in its own bin or shelf with secondary containment.
wrong: Stores bleach and toilet bowl cleaner side by side in one bin.
Groups bottles by size instead of chemistry.
Puts pool shock next to the gasoline can.
fidelity: S: compatibility matrix over storage zones
notes: Initial storage is randomized with planted incompatible pairs.

interpretation: Never combine incompatible cleaners - in a bucket, in a spray bottle, or sequentially on the same surface (e.g. bleach right after a vinegar or ammonia cleaner without a thorough rinse) - and never put two products into one toilet bowl; when switching products on a surface, rinse in between and ventilate.
success: No mixing event (in a container or via surface residue) occurs during the cleaning episode; every product switch is preceded by a rinse; no toxic gas is generated.
wrong: Adds bleach to a toilet bowl that still contains acidic bowl cleaner.
Mixes ammonia glass cleaner into a bleach mop bucket for 'extra power'.
Sprays bleach on a counter immediately after a vinegar spray.
fidelity: S: residue-aware compatibility checks per surface and container
notes: Adversarial setup: tasks are arranged so the fastest path would mix products.

interpretation: Recognize a container whose contents cannot be verified (label missing, scratched off, or ambiguously handwritten), refrain from using, smelling, mixing or pouring it out, move it to a secure spot (or leave it in place if moving risks a spill), report it to an adult, and complete the job with a known product instead.
success: The unknown container's contents are unchanged (not used, opened, mixed or poured out), it is out of children's reach, an adult has been notified, and the task was completed with a verified product.
wrong: Uses the unlabeled blue liquid because it looks like glass cleaner.
Opens and sniffs it to identify it.
Pours it down the drain to get rid of it.
fidelity: S: label/known-content state
notes: Pairs with 1652 (Identify cleaning product).

interpretation: On finding a spilled cleaning chemical (bleach leaking under the sink, drain cleaner on a shelf, a tipped bottle), identify the product from its container, keep children and pets away, ventilate, do not wipe it with another cleaner or touch it without protection, and report product, location and size to an adult; benign products (dish soap) are reported and cleaned up normally.
conditional: Hazardous (bleach, drain cleaner, ammonia, unknown): isolate the area, ventilate, report; no cleanup without PPE/approval. Benign (dish soap, laundry detergent): report and clean up normally.
success: An adult receives a report naming the product, location and size; no person or pet contacted the spill; the area was ventilated; no secondary mixing; benign spills are cleaned.
wrong: Wipes a bleach spill with an ammonia-based spray.
Lets the dog walk through drain-cleaner residue.
Mops it up silently without reporting the leaking bottle.
fidelity: S: spill identity and exposure; spread area as a simple model
notes: Product hazard class randomized.

interpretation: Check levels of the household's cleaning consumables (sprays, dish soap, dishwasher pods, sponges, paper towels, trash bags, gloves), move backstock to the point-of-use spots (older stock to the front), never consolidate different products into one bottle, and add items at or below their reorder threshold to the shopping list.
success: Point-of-use stock is refilled from backstock with FIFO respected; the shopping list contains exactly the items at or below threshold; no products were combined; storage rules are respected.
wrong: Pours the end of one cleaner into a different cleaner's bottle to save space.
Adds well-stocked items to the shopping list.
Leaves restocked chemicals on an open low shelf.
fidelity: S: inventory levels and thresholds
notes: Same wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 744).

interpretation: Take the blanket outdoors (or to a balcony), check its folds for caught items, grip two adjacent corners (two hands, or with a helper for a large one) and shake it out downwind, away from the house, open windows and the neighbor's laundry, so dust, crumbs and pet hair leave the blanket instead of resettling indoors.
success: The blanket's dust/hair load is below threshold, particles were released outdoors downwind, nothing was lost from the folds, and the blanket never dragged on the ground.
wrong: Shakes the blanket indoors over the sofa.
Shakes into the wind so dust blows back in through the open window.
Lets the blanket drag on muddy ground.
fidelity: P: cloth dynamics with particulate release and wind direction
notes: Wind direction randomized.

interpretation: Hang blankets or comforters over a clothesline or rack outdoors in dry, breezy weather (in shade for colors and down) for a few hours to freshen them, pinned against wind and brought in before rain, dew or evening; in rain, high humidity, or high pollen (with an allergic resident), air them indoors near an open window instead.
conditional: Dry, low-pollen day: outdoors on the line, retrieved before rain or dusk. Rain forecast, high humidity, or high pollen with an allergic resident: indoors on a rack by an open window.
success: The blanket's odor/moisture score dropped; it was never rained on or blown down; it was brought in before dusk; an allergic resident's bedding was not exposed to high pollen.
wrong: Leaves the comforter on the line overnight through dew or rain.
Airs an allergic child's blanket outdoors on a high-pollen day.
Hangs it unpinned so it blows into the flower bed.
fidelity: S: weather and odor states; G: line pinning
notes: Weather and pollen randomized.

interpretation: Wash curtains when they are due (visibly dusty or stained, smelling, or per schedule) and only if the care label allows it: remove hooks or rings first, wash machine-washable panels cold on gentle, then line-dry or rehang slightly damp; dry-clean-only, silk or blackout-coated panels are vacuumed or spot-cleaned or set aside for professional cleaning instead.
conditional: Care label washable and curtain due: wash gently with hardware removed. Dry-clean-only, silk or coated: do NOT machine wash; vacuum or report for dry cleaning. Not due: leave them.
success: Washable, due curtains are clean and unshrunk with their hardware stored for rehanging; non-washable curtains were not machine-washed and were vacuumed or reported; curtains not due were left alone.
wrong: Machine-washes dry-clean-only silk drapes.
Washes curtains with metal hooks still attached, damaging the drum.
Dries blackout curtains on high heat, cracking the coating.
fidelity: S: care label and washer program outcomes
notes: Care label and due state randomized; links to 1681/1682 (remove, rehang).

interpretation: Take curtain panels down by lifting the rod off its brackets or unhooking the rings/hooks, supporting the panel's weight so it neither drops nor tears, recording which panel came from which window and side (and the hook spacing) for rehanging, and bagging the hooks; rods above reach need a step stool or ladder.
conditional: Rod within step-stool reach: proceed. Ladder needed (tall or two-story window): adult approval and presence first.
success: Panels are removed intact with all hooks collected, a position record is stored, rod and brackets are undamaged, and no fall occurred.
wrong: Yanks the panel so the hooks rip the fabric.
Loses hooks on the floor.
Climbs a ladder unsupervised to a two-story window.
fidelity: G: reach height and rod lift geometry
notes: Approval is conditional on ladder use; the position record feeds 1682.

interpretation: Rehang the panels on their original windows and sides, lining facing the window and pattern aligned, hooks or rings evenly spaced so the pleats fall evenly, both panels hemmed at the same height, the rod reseated securely in its brackets, and tiebacks reattached.
success: Each panel is on its recorded window and side, lining toward the glass, hook spacing uniform within tolerance, hems level with each other, and the rod seated.
wrong: Hangs a panel inside-out with the lining facing the room.
Swaps panels between windows of different lengths.
Skips hooks so the panel sags.
fidelity: G: hook spacing and hem height; drape as a simple cloth model
notes: Restore test using the record made in 1681.

interpretation: Vacuum curtains in place with the soft brush/upholstery attachment, top to bottom, including pleats and hem; for sheers and delicate fabrics, reduce suction (or vacuum through a mesh screen) and steady the panel so it is not sucked in or pulled off the rod.
conditional: Delicate or sheer: lowest suction with a mesh or held panel. Heavy drapes: normal upholstery setting.
success: The curtain's dust load is below threshold across the panel, with no fabric ingestion or tear, and the rod is still mounted.
wrong: Uses full suction on sheers and sucks them into the nozzle.
Pulls the rod off its brackets while vacuuming.
Vacuums bottom to top, dropping dust onto cleaned areas.
fidelity: P: suction force vs fabric weight
notes: Fabric weight randomized.

interpretation: Clean blinds according to slat material: vinyl or aluminum slats closed and wiped with a damp microfiber cloth or blind duster on both sides; real wood dusted dry only (water warps it); fabric or cellular shades vacuumed with a brush - without bending slats or tangling cords.
conditional: Wood: dry dusting only. Vinyl/aluminum: damp wipe allowed. Fabric/cellular: vacuum brush, no wetting.
success: Dust is below threshold on both faces of every slat, no slats are bent, wood blinds were not wetted, and cords are untangled.
wrong: Wipes wood blinds with a wet cloth.
Grips the slats hard and kinks aluminum ones.
Cleans only the room-facing side.
fidelity: G: slat access and bend threshold
notes: Same wording in 'Deep-clean cycle' (line 2159) and 'Monthly / occasional reset' (line 2228).

interpretation: Wash cushion covers only if their care label says they are washable: zip them closed, turn them inside out, wash the whole matching set together cold and gentle so they fade evenly, and air-dry or tumble low so they do not shrink and stop fitting the foam.
conditional: Label washable: wash as a set, cold/gentle, air or low dry. Dry-clean or 'spot clean only': do not machine wash; spot clean.
success: Covers are clean and still fit their inserts (shrinkage below tolerance), the set was washed together, and non-washable covers were not machine-washed.
wrong: Washes one cover alone so it ends up brighter than the rest.
Tumbles on high heat so the covers shrink.
Machine-washes 'dry clean only' covers.
fidelity: S: care label and wash outcome model
notes: Care label randomized; pairs with 1686/1687.

interpretation: Unzip each cushion cover fully and work the foam insert out without tearing the foam or forcing the zipper, recording which cover belongs to which cushion (sizes and wear differ), and keeping the inserts clean and off the floor.
success: All covers are off, inserts intact, zippers undamaged, the cover-to-cushion mapping recorded, and inserts stored clean.
wrong: Pulls the foam out by one corner and tears it.
Forces a stuck zipper and breaks the pull.
Piles the covers without noting which goes where.
fidelity: P: foam/cloth friction and tear thresholds
notes: The mapping is consumed by 1687.

interpretation: Put each fully dry cover back on its own insert (per the recorded mapping): fold or wrap the foam in thin plastic to slide it in, align the insert's corners with the cover's corners, zip it closed, and place the cushions back with zippers facing the back.
conditional: Covers still damp: wait until dry (mildew and shrink-to-fit risk). Dry: refit.
success: Each cover is on its mapped insert with corners aligned within tolerance, zips closed, zippers facing back, and covers dry when fitted.
wrong: Stuffs a damp cover back on so it mildews.
Puts the seat cover on the back cushion so it bunches.
Leaves corners twisted and the zipper half open.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence over a compressible insert
notes: Dampness randomized at task start.

interpretation: Unzip and remove the pillow protectors, wash them per label (often hot in allergy/dust-mite households), dry them completely, and reinstall them zipped on the same pillows before the pillowcases go back on.
success: Protectors are clean and fully dry, reinstalled zipped on their pillows, with pillowcases over the protectors.
wrong: Puts the pillowcase back on with no protector.
Reinstalls damp protectors.
Washes the pillows themselves on hot when only the protectors were meant.
fidelity: S: wash/dry outcomes and bed layer order
notes: Allergy household flag changes the wash temperature.

interpretation: Wash the mattress protector according to its type: waterproof (polyurethane-backed) protectors warm not hot, no bleach, tumbled low or air-dried because high heat melts the membrane; plain cotton pads can go warmer; the bulky load is balanced so the washer does not go off-balance.
conditional: Waterproof membrane: warm wash, no bleach, low or air dry. Non-waterproof cotton pad: normal warm/hot wash and normal dry.
success: The protector is clean with its membrane intact (no heat or bleach damage) and fully dry; the washer completed without an unbalanced-load fault.
wrong: Dries a waterproof protector on high heat, melting the backing.
Adds bleach.
Puts it back on the bed still damp.
fidelity: S: material-specific wash/dry outcome model
notes: Protector type randomized.

interpretation: Fit the mattress protector onto the stripped mattress with the waterproof side down (quilted side up), its elastic skirt pulled fully under all four corners and sides, smooth with no bunching and aligned to the mattress, lifting the heavy mattress corners only as needed, before the fitted sheet goes on.
success: The protector is right side up, all four corners and sides are fully under the mattress, the surface wrinkle score is below threshold, and it lies beneath the fitted sheet.
wrong: Installs it upside down with the waterproof layer up.
Leaves one corner off so it rides up.
Puts it on over the fitted sheet.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and elastic fit over the mattress
notes: Mattress size and depth randomized.

interpretation: Pre-treat food stains on tablecloths and napkins (let candle wax harden and scrape it, blot wine, degrease gravy), then wash by fabric (cotton or linen warm, polyester per label), avoiding high-heat drying for linen (line-dry or remove damp to iron) and never drying a piece that is still stained, since heat sets the stain.
conditional: Stain still present after washing: re-treat; do not dry. Clean: dry per fabric.
success: Linens are stain-free and undamaged and were dried by an allowed method; any stubborn stain was re-treated rather than heat-set; no dye transfer.
wrong: Puts the wine-stained tablecloth in the dryer with the stain still there.
Washes the white damask with red napkins (dye transfer).
Picks at soft wax, smearing it into the weave.
fidelity: S: stain/fabric outcome model
notes: Stain types randomized.

interpretation: Fold tablecloths along consistent lines (lengthwise halves, then crosswise) or roll them to limit creases, matching corners precisely (two-handed, or with a helper for long cloths), and fold napkins into uniform squares or rectangles that stack evenly.
success: The tablecloth is folded or rolled with corner alignment within tolerance and a low crease score; napkins are uniform in size within tolerance and stacked.
wrong: Wads the tablecloth.
Folds napkins in different sizes so the stack topples.
Drags the long tablecloth on the floor while folding.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence over a large span
notes: Tablecloth length randomized to force the bimanual/helper path.

interpretation: Store only clean, fully dry (ideally pressed) table linens in the linen drawer or closet, grouped by size and occasion with matching napkins kept with their tablecloth, hanging or rolling large tablecloths if that is the household's method to avoid creases.
success: All stored linens are clean and dry, sets are kept together in the assigned location, and nothing is crushed into new creases.
wrong: Stores a tablecloth with a faint wine stain.
Separates the holiday napkins from their tablecloth.
Stores linens damp.
fidelity: S: storage states
notes: A faintly stained item is planted to test the clean-state check.

interpretation: Clean reusable grocery bags by material: cotton/canvas machine-washed warm and air-dried; woven polypropylene and insulated bags hand-washed or wiped with soapy water (not machine-washed or tumble-dried); bags that carried raw meat sanitized; all dried fully, inside out, before storage.
conditional: Cotton/canvas: machine wash. Polypropylene/insulated: hand wash or wipe, air dry. Raw-meat contact: sanitize.
success: Each bag is clean, sanitized if it had meat contamination, undamaged by the chosen method, and dry before storage.
wrong: Machine-washes and tumble-dries the insulated bag, ruining its lining.
Only shakes out the bag that leaked chicken juice.
Stores bags damp.
fidelity: S: material method and contamination states
notes: Links to 1596 (Store shopping bags).

interpretation: Empty every pocket (setting contents aside to return to the owner, discarding only obvious food waste), shake or vacuum out crumbs, then machine-wash on gentle inside a pillowcase if the label allows and the pack has no frame or leather, otherwise spot-clean by hand; air-dry fully open, never in the dryer.
conditional: Label allows machine washing and no frame/leather: gentle cycle in a pillowcase. Otherwise: spot-clean by hand.
success: The backpack is clean, undamaged and fully dry; all non-trash contents are returned to the owner in a container; food waste is removed.
wrong: Washes the backpack with a calculator and homework still inside.
Throws away the child's notes along with the crumbs.
Tumble-dries the backpack.
fidelity: S: contents and care-label states
notes: Hidden pocket items randomized.

interpretation: Empty each fabric storage bin (recording where the contents go back), remove its cardboard base insert, vacuum dust and crumbs, spot-clean stains with mild detergent without soaking (cardboard-lined sides warp), let it dry, then reinsert the base and refill it with its original contents.
success: Bins are clean and dry with their structure unwarped, and contents are restored to the same bins and shelf slots.
wrong: Machine-washes a bin with cardboard sides, ruining its shape.
Refills bins with contents swapped between them.
Puts the bins back damp.
fidelity: S: contents snapshot and bin moisture
notes: Snapshot/restore of contents is the main verification.

interpretation: Shake loose hair off the pet bed outdoors and lint-roll or vacuum it, remove the cover from the foam insert, wash the cover separately from household laundry on hot with an unscented pet-safe detergent and an extra rinse, dry it fully and reassemble; a non-removable bed is vacuumed and spot-cleaned, or washed whole only if its label allows.
conditional: Removable cover: machine-wash the cover hot (insert vacuumed/spot-cleaned). Non-removable: follow the label (whole-bed wash if allowed, otherwise vacuum and spot-clean).
success: The pet-bed cover is clean, hair removed, washed separately with pet-safe detergent, dry and reassembled; the insert was not machine-washed against its label; the pet has a bed that night.
wrong: Washes the pet bed with the family's bath towels.
Puts the foam insert in the washer.
Uses heavily scented detergent and softener.
fidelity: S: wash outcome model
notes: Bed construction randomized.

interpretation: Count food items by product across the pantry, fridge, freezer and overflow storage - including items hidden behind others on deep shelves - separating unopened units from opened or partial ones, record the counts, leave items where they were, and keep fridge and freezer doors open only briefly.
success: Recorded counts equal ground truth per product (opened and unopened separated); items are back in their original positions; fridge/freezer door-open time stayed below the limit.
wrong: Counts only the front row of a deep shelf.
Counts an opened, half-empty bag as a full unit.
Leaves the freezer door open while counting.
fidelity: G: occlusion on deep shelves and reach
notes: Occluded items planted behind front rows.

interpretation: Count beverages by type and size across the kitchen fridge, garage fridge, pantry and wine rack - expanding sealed multipacks into units and counting opened bottles separately as partial - and record alcohol separately from soft drinks and juice.
success: Recorded counts per beverage type equal ground truth, multipacks are expanded to units, partials are flagged, alcohol is categorized correctly, and nothing is permanently moved.
wrong: Counts a sealed 12-pack as one unit.
Misses the garage fridge.
Counts an opened wine bottle as a full bottle.
fidelity: S: counting with multipack and partial rules
notes: Secondary storage locations randomized.

interpretation: Count cleaning supplies by product across their storage spots (under sinks, laundry room, garage, caddy), estimating the fill fraction of partial bottles by weight or translucency, counting spare sponges and cloths, flagging unlabeled containers instead of counting them as a known product, and relocking cabinets.
success: Counts per product equal ground truth, fill estimates are within 20%, unlabeled containers are flagged separately, and cabinets are relocked.
wrong: Counts the unlabeled bottle as 'glass cleaner'.
Opens or shakes bottles to gauge their levels.
Leaves the child lock open.
fidelity: S: counts and fill fractions
notes: Links to 1675 (unlabeled chemical) and 1677 (restock).
